propositions: A store write whose lock acquisition times out is discarded with no retry, causing permanent data loss instead of queueing or retry.
The acquire() function computes a single deadline from timeout*attempts, where attempts acts as a multiplier rather than a retry loop.
Both fcntl and mkdir lock legs use non-blocking polling with jitter, providing no fairness or FIFO ordering among waiters.
Holder duration (not writer count) is now the primary trigger for loss; a single holder exceeding the 60s budget causes all waiters to fail regardless of service order.
Bounded retry-with-backoff inside acquire() converts lock timeout from permanent loss into bounded latency, with retries parameter defaulting to 0 for backward compatibility.
Five call sites opted into retries (event_append.py 3x, txn.py 1x, push.py 1x) while all others keep fail-fast behavior unchanged via retries=0 default.
